en.name: Broth, homemade
en.summary: Homemade broth is a low-acid, protein-rich liquid with nothing added to preserve it, which makes it one of the more perishable things a kitchen produces. Refrigerated it keeps 3–4 days. Frozen it holds about 2–3 months of good quality, and freezing is what makes a big batch worth making.
en.pantry: Broth must never be stored at room temperature, and the most common mistake is leaving the stockpot on the stove to cool overnight. A deep pot of hot broth stays inside the 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) danger zone for hours. Get it out of that range fast: divide it into shallow containers, or sit the pot in a sink of iced water and stir. Then refrigerate or freeze it within two hours of cooking, one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Cooled and covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, homemade broth keeps 3–4 days. Leave the fat cap on if there is one — it seals the surface and lifts off cleanly when you want it. Store it in a container you can see into, and reheat only the portion you need, bringing it to a full rolling boil each time rather than warming it through. Reheating the whole batch repeatedly wastes its short life.
en.freezer: Freezing is the point of making broth in quantity. Cool it first, then fill rigid containers or flat-laid bags at −18 °C (0 °F), leaving headspace because liquid expands, and expect about 2–3 months of good quality. Frozen food held at that temperature stays safe indefinitely; the limit is flavour. Freeze in the portions you actually cook with, and freeze a tray of cubes for the splash a pan sauce needs.
en.thawing: Thaw broth in the fridge, or drop the frozen block straight into a hot pan. Never thaw it on the counter, and bring it to a rolling boil before using thawed broth.
spoilage: A sour, sharp or fermented smell
Ropy or slimy strands when you stir it, or a stickiness on the spoon
Bubbles, fizzing or a lid that has domed up
Mould on the surface or on the fat cap
tips: Cool it fast in shallow containers, never overnight on the stove.
Label every container with the contents and the date.
Freeze cubes for pan sauces and larger portions for soups.
Reduce a batch before freezing to save space, and dilute it back when you use it.

faq.q: How long does homemade broth last in the fridge?
faq.a: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, cooled quickly and covered.
Yes, and you should. Cool it, portion it with headspace and freeze at −18 °C for about 2–3 months of good quality.

faq.q: Can you leave broth on the stove to cool overnight?
faq.a: No. A deep pot stays in the danger zone for hours. Cool it in shallow containers or an ice bath and refrigerate within two hours.

faq.q: Does boiling old broth make it safe again?
faq.a: No. Boiling kills bacteria but does not remove the toxins some of them leave behind. If it smells sour or looks ropy, discard it.

zh.name: 自製高湯
zh.summary: 自製高湯是低酸、富含蛋白質的液體，而且沒有任何防腐成分，是廚房裡最容易變質的產物之一。冷藏 3～4 天。冷凍風味大約可維持 2～3 個月——而冷凍正是「一次熬一大鍋」值得的理由。
zh.pantry: 高湯絕對不能放室溫，最常見的錯誤就是把湯鍋留在爐上放涼過夜。一深鍋熱湯會在 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶裡停留好幾個小時。請快速讓它離開這個區間：分裝到淺容器，或把鍋子坐在裝冰水的水槽裡並持續攪拌。然後在煮好後兩小時內冷藏或冷凍，廚房超過 32 °C 時縮短為一小時。
zh.fridge: 放涼加蓋後放 4 °C 以下，自製高湯可放 3～4 天。表面如果有一層凝固的油脂，就留著——它會封住表面，要用時整片掀掉很乾淨。裝在看得見內容物的容器裡，每次只加熱要用的份量，而且每次都要煮到大滾，不要只是溫熱。整鍋反覆加熱只會浪費它本來就很短的壽命。
zh.freezer: 冷凍才是熬一大鍋高湯的意義所在。先放涼，再裝進硬質容器或平放的密封袋放 −18 °C，記得留膨脹空間，風味大約可維持 2～3 個月。食物在這個溫度下安全性可以無限期維持，限制的是風味。請按實際下廚會用到的份量分裝，另外凍一盤高湯冰塊，做鍋底醬時只需要一點點。
zh.thawing: 高湯請放冷藏解凍，或直接把凍塊丟進熱鍋。絕對不要放室溫解凍，解凍後使用前要煮到大滾。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸、刺鼻或有發酵味
攪動時出現絲狀或黏稠感，湯匙上黏黏的
冒泡、有氣體，或蓋子鼓起
tips: 用淺容器快速降溫，絕對不要留在爐上過夜。
每個容器都標示內容物和日期。
小份凍成冰塊做醬汁，大份分裝煮湯。
冷凍前先收乾一點可以省空間，使用時再加水稀釋回來。

faq.q: 自製高湯放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 快速放涼、加蓋後放 4 °C 以下，可放 3～4 天。
可以，而且很推薦。放涼、留膨脹空間分裝後放 −18 °C，風味大約可維持 2～3 個月。

faq.q: 高湯可以留在爐上放涼過夜嗎？
faq.a: 不行。深鍋會在危險溫度帶停留好幾個小時。請用淺容器或冰水浴降溫，並在兩小時內冷藏。

faq.q: 放太久的高湯再煮沸就沒問題了嗎？
faq.a: 不是。煮沸能殺死細菌，但無法去除某些細菌留下的毒素。聞起來發酸或變得黏稠就要丟掉。
